claims.text: On the 6 pilot sessions, SPY's quoted spread was 1 cent for most of the time in every strategy window; the time-weighted half-spread was 0.12-0.25 bp per side.
That is below the base model's 0.5 bp half-spread assumption, so for the spread component only, on these ordinary days, the base assumption looks conservative (provisionally).
The measurement pipeline worked as pre-registered: 60 of 60 windows complete, no invalid, duplicate or out-of-order records, well inside the request and storage caps.
It says nothing about stressed or high-volatility days: none of the 6 randomly chosen sessions was a known stress day, and spreads widen exactly when costs matter most.
It does not measure slippage (0.5 bp per side at base) or the sell fee: quotes are not fills, so most of the 2.3 bp base round trip remains unmeasured.
It cannot change the cost model or any closed verdict: the pilot itself states it is not reliable enough to change trading/costs.py, and running the remaining 18 calm sessions would not make it so.
Every measured quote carries the undocumented condition code '?', and the timestamp clock and NBBO construction are undocumented, so the numbers are labelled, not verified.

Five questions remain open with Alpaca (A1 timestamp clock, A2 condition '?', A3 consolidated-quote construction, A4 locked/crossed meaning, A5 filtering/corrections); the support request is drafted and unsent - sending it is the owner's decision.
The same answers gate the deferred gap-down candidate, which stays DEFERRED_DATA_SEMANTICS (never evaluated on performance) until all five are answered in writing.
